blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets on your Mac

Since Google Sheets is a web app, you do not have a native installer. For the best performance on a Mac, use Google Chrome. Open sheets.google.com in Chrome. Click the three dots in the top right corner. Go to Cast, Save, and Share. Select Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder. Now you can launch Sheets like a real app. It stays in your Dock. It does not get lost in a sea of browser tabs.

Your job involves constant data imports from HubSpot or Salesforce. You must clean these exports before you can use them. First, handle duplicates. Use the built-in tools to keep your lists clean. If you need to split text into columns, use the Data menu. Always check for trailing spaces in your cells. They break lookup formulas every time. If a formula returns #N/A, check for those hidden spaces first.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for your Mac

Memorizing these saves you from constant trackpad use. When you are deep in a report, keeping your hands on the keyboard is vital. If you forget a shortcut, just press ⌘ + / to open the menu. You can search for any action there.

Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. Even with that capacity, large sheets get slow. Do not keep too many heavy formulas in one tab. If you have a massive dataset, use ImportRange to pull data from other files. This keeps your main file snappy. If you hit the limit, it is time to move that data to BigQuery or another database. Do not force Sheets to do what it cannot handle.
When to ask Lazur for help

Lazur is a voice assistant for your Mac. It sits in your notch. When you are stuck in a complex spreadsheet, you do not need to switch to a browser tab to search for help. Hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask your question. Lazur sees your screen. It can point to the menu item you need. It can explain how to write a specific formula. It keeps you focused on your work.

items: Editing the raw export file directly. Always keep a copy of the original data.
Using complex nested formulas that are hard to debug. Break them into smaller steps.
Sharing files without checking the access permissions. Use the Share button to verify who can see your data.
Ignoring the revision history. You can always go back if you make a mistake.
Leaving sensitive data in public sheets. Check your sharing settings often.

blocks.text: Marketing operations is about process. Use a consistent naming convention for your files. Store them in organized folders. If you work with a team, document your formulas in a separate tab. Explain what each column means. This helps others understand your work. It also helps you when you return to a file after three months.

Sheets is excellent for real-time collaboration. Use comments to ask questions. Tag your team members with @mention. This keeps the conversation inside the file. It saves you from sending emails. If you have too many people editing at once, performance will drop. Keep your active collaborators to a small group.

Your Mac is a tool. Your browser is a tool. Google Sheets is a tool. Use them together to get your work done. Do not let the small things slow you down. If you need to find a setting, ask Lazur. If you need to type a long note, use dictation. Keep your setup clean. Keep your data clean. You will spend less time on admin and more time on strategy.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop application for macOS. You can create a Progressive Web App (PWA) shortcut using Google Chrome to get a similar experience.

faq.question: How do I fix formula errors in Sheets?
faq.answer: Start by checking your cell ranges. Look for missing commas or quotes. Use the built-in formula help by hovering over the error. If you are still stuck, ask Lazur to explain the error.

faq.question: What is the cell limit in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the limit is 20 million cells per spreadsheet.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my spreadsheet directly?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you, points at interface elements, and answers your questions out loud.
